summary: inventory-api is running persistently on node1 at port 8080. A controlled global OOM killed the memory hog while the API remained available without restarting. The service also recovered successfully after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled inventory-api.service with Restart=always.
Configured OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 and a 64 MiB protected memory reservation.
Verified /healthz and /inventory through node1's managed IP.
Triggered controlled global OOM pressure with memory-hog at OOMScoreAdjust=1000.
Confirmed the kernel killed memory-hog while inventory-api retained its PID and zero restarts.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified service persistence and API recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a protected managed service
evidence.summary: Shows inventory-api enabled and active, listening on port 8080, responding successfully, and running with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, Restart=always, and 64 MiB MemoryMin/MemoryLow.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api continues serving under memory pressure
evidence.summary: Shows the API responding during pressure and afterward with unchanged PID 2438 and zero restarts.

evidence.requirement: The kernel stops the memory hog during system OOM
evidence.summary: Kernel evidence identifies a global OOM and confirms memory-hog PID 2487 was killed with oom_score_adj=1000; its systemd result is oom-kill.

Captures the healthy pre-restart baseline and boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID from 984a7d52-3387-4830-a06e-15e8b5e6c2a1 to 2a158d03-809e-4489-aefe-d0e6dcb540c5, and recovered active service, listener, protection settings, and HTTP responses.
